stem: For a 25-year old man with severe aplastic anemia had disease relapse 8 months after immunosuppressive therapy (IST) using rabbit ATG + Cyclosporine. The patient does not have HLA-matched sibling donor but have a 10/10 matched unrelated donor (MUD). Which of the following is the treatment of choice for his condition?

options.A: Repeat IST with Horse ATG + Cyclosporin
options.B: Repeat IST with Eltrombopag + horse ATG + Cyclosporin

stem: Which of the following statement about severe aplastic anemia(SAA) is wrong?

options.A: Incidences of relapse and clonal evolution of SAA patient treated with immunosuppressive therapy(IST) plus Eltrombopag were similar to historical experience with IST alone.
options.B: The SAA patients receive early bone marrow HCT with conditioning regimen of ATG plus Cyclophosphamide, and GVHD prophylaxis combining Cyclosporine and MTX have a high risk of secondary malignancy.
options.C: Adding Eltrombopag to IST for SAA patients increases the overall response rate.
options.D: Adding Eltrombopag to IST for SAA patients increases transfusion independency and provides similar safety.

stem: Which of the following statements for paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria is wrong?

options.A: Eculizumab has proven to be effective in inhibiting intravascular hemolysis of PNH, leading to hemoglobin stabilization and transfusion independency in about half of patients.
options.B: Ravulizumab was shown to be non-inferior to Eculizumab in terms of LDH normalization, transfusion avoidance, breakthrough hemolysis, hemoglobin stabilization and patient-reported outcome.
options.C: In adult PNH patients with baseline hemoglobin < 10.5 g/dl after 3-month Eculizumab treatment and receiving 4-week Pegcetacoplan plus Eculizumab, subsequent Pegacetacoplan monotherapy was superior to Eculizumab monotherapy in terms of hemoglobin change from baseline.
options.D: Eculizumab treatment has no improvement of overall survival in PNH patients

stem: Which of the following statement about HSCT for acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) is wrong?

options.A: Fractionated total body irradiation (TBI) in combination with cyclophosphamide as the conditioning therapy is only recommended in patients with ALL younger than 45 years of age, not in those elder than 45.
options.B: For patients with Ph+ ALL, maintenance with the tyrosine kinase inhibitor after allo-HSCT should be applied as a prophylactic or preemptive therapy.
options.C: For haplo-HSCT, using T cell replete allografts combined with post-transplant cyclophosphamide is an established option for patients with ALL.
options.D: Auto-HSCT is optional for patients with MRD-negative high-risk ALL, not eligible for allo-HSCT.
options.E: Before the advent of CAR-T therapy, allo-HSCT is the only potentially curative treatment option for adults with relapsed or refractory (R/R) B-cell ALL.

stem:
Regarding SOS/VOD prophylaxis and treatment which statement are correct?
(1) Defibrotide remains the only agent for the treatment of severe SOS/VOD and should be initiated as soon as possible in those patients,
(2) Given that early treatment initiation is associated with a higher day +100 OS,
(3) Regarding prophylaxis, for the pharmacologic measures, ursodeoxycholic acid administered from initiation of conditioning until day +90 after transplantation is recommended in adults.
(4) Regarding the use of prophylactic defibrotide, a prospective randomized phase III clinical trial compared defibrotide versus best supportive care for prevention of SOS/VOD in 372 pediatric and adult patients at high risk of SOS/VOD after transplantation (NCT02851407). Significant difference was observed between defibrotide and best supportive care groups in the primary end point.
